title: Actor-capability mapping and sentinel scopes for RBAC v2
creator: Samira Patel
description: Background: RBAC v1 mixes coarse roles with tenant-agnostic authorities. We need RBAC v2 that expresses fine-grained actor->capability mappings with conditional constraints (time, region, data-sensitivity). This ticket designs the core model: an actor-capability mapping, 'sentinel' scopes (scopes that impose conditional constraints evaluated at request time), and an enforcement contract that enables SSO/SAML attribute mapping and comprehensive audit logging. Goals: 1) express permissions as (actor, capability, resource-pattern, sentinel-scopes), 2) deterministic evaluation order with fallback safe-deny, 3) efficient caching viable for high-volume serving paths, 4) compatibility with SAML attribute-based role assertions and existing role mappings, and 5) audit trails that capture scope evaluation context for post-incident analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Design document describing actor-capability mapping and sentinel scope schema reviewed and approved by security and infra
Evaluation algorithm defined with complexity analysis and caching invalidation semantics
SAML attribute mapping examples included for IdPs used by top 5 customers
Audit log schema specified (immutable event per evaluation) and sample events produced by emulator
Migration mapping for top 20 existing roles to new capability sets documented
End-to-end prototype: auth-check endpoints exercising sentinel scopes with perf < 1.5x current check latency under representative load
design_decisions: Model: split identity (actor) and capability; capabilities are immutable strings with annotation metadata for required scope parameters
Sentinel scopes: evaluators that add conditional constraints (example: region==eu || time-window==maintenance-window) and return (allow|deny|conditional) with reason codes
Evaluation order: 1) explicit deny rules, 2) scoped allows with highest specificity (resource pattern length), 3) tenant-level defaults, 4) global fallback deny
Permission leash: every allow must indicate an enforcement leash (max duration, allowed resource pattern, token scoping) to power short-lived delegation and auditability
Caching: cache positive allows keyed by (actor, capability, resource-hash, scope-version), TTL short (30s) with immediate invalidation on role-change hooks from control plane
SAML: IdP-to-capability mapping performed by a mapping table that can be updated via console; SAML assertions may populate sentinel scope attributes (e.g., department, org_unit, region)

Audit logging: log every evaluation with actor, capability, resource, sentinel-eval-results, policy-version, request-trace-id. Logs are append-only and forwarded to our observability pipeline with structured fields for slicing.

Admin controls: breakglass tokens that bypass sentinel scopes but are issued with stricter audit leash (short TTL, mandatory approval workflows), and delegated admin boundaries scoped to resource prefixes
migration_plan: Inventory existing roles and map to capability primitives (script: tooling/role-mapper-v1-to-v2) - iteration 1 target: top 20 roles by usage
Create compatibility layer: accept old role names in SAML mapping that translate to capability lists until deprecation
Canary rollout: enable RBAC v2 evaluation for 5% of requests with A/B flag; monitor false-deny and false-allow rates
Fallback: on unexpected failures, automatic fail-open to v1 evaluation for read-only paths; fail-closed for mutating paths
Deprecation timeline: 90 days canary -> 60 days staged -> 30 days enforcement for non-sensitive tenants
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: design review, security signoff, and prototyping of sentinel scope evaluators
Week 3-4: implement policy evaluation library and audit log schema; internal alpha with synthetic traffic
Week 5-6: SAML mapping UI + control plane hooks; run migration script for two internal tenants
Week 7-8: Canary release to 5% production traffic; monitor metrics: auth-latency, auth-error-rate, audit-event-size, false-deny-rate
Week 9+: progressive traffic ramp and customer opt-ins; final enforcement switch after stability gate

risks: Performance: extra evaluation cost could increase tail latency on hot paths
Complexity: overly flexible sentinel expressions could become un-auditable and lead to policy sprawl
Backward compatibility: translation mismatches could cause customer outages during migration
Operational: audit log volume increase and storage cost if every evaluation is logged naively
Security: breakglass misuse if approval workflows are not robust
mitigations: Performance: precompile common sentinel predicates and micro-cache results; add optimized fast-path in serving runtime
Complexity: introduce policy linter and a console policy catalogue with recommended patterns
Backward compatibility: staged translation with safety nets (automatic role rollback based on error budgets)
Operational: sample non-critical evaluations and compress audit payloads; add retention tiers
Security: breakglass requires two-person approval and generates immediate alert to on-call channel
